title: Cost-related care foregoing is a population-level choice stage absent from observed-care files
source_unit: US adult respondent; 2025 Federal Reserve SHED published report

observations.period: 2025; any medical treatment skipped because of cost
observations.method: Federal Reserve SHED 2025 published Table 22 and Health-Care Expenses narrative.
observations.uncertainty: Rounded self-reported cross-sectional percentage; no event date, causal design, or follow-up outcome.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported foregoing may reflect illness, access, coverage, provider availability, deductible, travel, or other constraints rather than one bill alone.

observations.period: 2025; care type skipped because of cost
observations.method: Federal Reserve SHED 2025 published Table 22; respondents could select multiple treatment types.
observations.uncertainty: Rounded self-reported overlapping categories; no exact bill, condition, date, or treatment outcome.
observations.counterinterpretation: Categories are not mutually exclusive and do not indicate which treatment was most clinically consequential.

observations.period: 2025; care skipped because of cost by family income

denominator.unit: adults in each published family-income group

under_25000.unit: percent of adults with family income under $25,000

at_least_100000.unit: percent of adults with family income at least $100,000

observations.method: Federal Reserve SHED 2025 published income comparison in the Health-Care Expenses section.
observations.uncertainty: Rounded descriptive income comparison; income, illness, coverage, access, and local supply are not jointly modeled.
observations.counterinterpretation: The income gradient does not identify whether cash, coverage, provider access, illness, or other differences produced the gap.

observations.period: 2025; care skipped because of cost by insurance status

denominator.unit: adults in each published insurance group

observations.method: Federal Reserve SHED 2025 published insurance comparison in the Health-Care Expenses section.
observations.uncertainty: Rounded descriptive insurance comparison; coverage type, plan design, health need, and access are not separated.
observations.subgroup: Published uninsured and insured adult groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Insurance does not guarantee affordable or timely care; uninsured/insured status is not a randomized exposure.

medical_debt.unit: percent with debt from own or family member medical care

observations.method: Federal Reserve SHED 2025 published Health-Care Expenses narrative.
observations.uncertainty: Debt may not be from the prior year and may concern a family member; no balance, creditor, date, or health outcome is reported here.
observations.counterinterpretation: Medical debt is a financial status, not proof of current care delay or a specific unpaid bill.

boundary: Published SHED evidence closes a population-level cost-related care-foregoing stage but does not establish a dated bill-to-choice-to-outcome episode, treatment quality, debt causation, recovery, remedy, trust, or political action.
